security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples in SKILL.md. No Ruby backtick execution, prompt injection, network reconnaissance, or system reconnaissance evidence was found. One medium operational risk remains because the skill documents a destructive Git reset command.

remediation.issue: Destructive Git reset guidance can discard local work.
remediation.suggestion: Remove git reset --hard guidance or require explicit user confirmation and a clean diff check before use.

remediation.issue: The skill includes commit and push examples after automatic fixes.
remediation.suggestion: State that commits and pushes require user approval after reviewing git diff and test results.

remediation.issue: Automatic formatting and linting can modify many files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer preview mode for broad changes and report every modified path before applying fixes.

content.user_title: Fix Python Formatting and Lint Issues
content.value_statement: Python quality checks often fail because formatting, imports, and lint fixes drift during development. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe cleanup and clear review steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides Black and isort formatting for Python source and test files.
Applies Ruff auto-fixes for safe lint issues such as unused imports.
Identifies Black and Ruff formatter conflicts and suggests manual resolutions.
Supports dry-run preview commands before modifying project files.
Produces a review report with changed files, fixes applied, and next steps.
limitations: Does not fix business logic, algorithm defects, or failing tests.
Does not infer complex type hints that require domain knowledge.
Does not write missing docstrings or improve documentation content.
Requires installed project tools such as Black, isort, Ruff, and make targets.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Before Commit
use_cases.description: Format Python files, sort imports, and remove safe lint issues before opening a change for review.

use_cases.title: Resolve Review Feedback
use_cases.description: Apply requested formatting and lint cleanup after a reviewer reports style or quality gate failures.

use_cases.title: Recover From CI Quality Failures
use_cases.description: Reproduce local quality checks, apply automatic fixes, and report remaining manual work.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Project Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup for an entire Python project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply safe quality fixes to this Python project. Format files, run lint auto-fixes, and show the changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Fix One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted cleanup for a single file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix formatting and safe lint issues in the file I specify. Show the diff summary and any remaining manual issues.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Fixes First
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview quality fixes for the Python source tree. Do not modify files until I confirm the proposed changes.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Formatter Conflicts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup when Black and Ruff disagree.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Black and Ruff formatter conflicts, explain each conflict, apply safe resolutions, and verify both tools pass.

output_examples.input: Quality checks failed after adding a new validator module.
output_examples.output: The skill formats changed Python files, removes safe unused imports, then reports remaining issues that need manual review.

output_examples.input: A pull request reviewer asked for import sorting and lint cleanup.
output_examples.output: The skill runs targeted formatting, applies safe Ruff fixes, and summarizes changed files for the reviewer.

output_examples.input: Black and Ruff disagree on a long error message.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests extracting the message into a variable, then verifies both formatting and lint checks again.

best_practices: Run preview commands before applying broad changes to a large repository.
Review the diff after every automatic formatting or linting pass.
Run tests after quality fixes to confirm behavior did not change.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive Git commands without explicit user confirmation.
Do not treat formatter success as proof that the code is correct.
Do not apply broad auto-fixes when generated or vendor files are not excluded.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill use?
faq.answer: It guides Black, isort, Ruff, make targets, and project quality checks when they are available.

faq.question: Can it fix failing tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on formatting, import sorting, lint auto-fixes, and formatter conflict cleanup.

faq.question: Does it change code automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide file changes through local tools, but users should review diffs before committing.

faq.question: Can it work on one file?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes targeted workflows for a single Python file or selected path.

faq.question: What happens when auto-fixes are unsafe?
faq.answer: The skill should report the issue and leave complex logic, types, and tests for manual work.

faq.question: Is it suitable for CI?
faq.answer: It can help reproduce CI failures locally, while CI should usually run checks without applying fixes.
